method: Direct bounded reading of primary printed editions. Reported third-witness readings remain attributed; no fresh original-photo or whole-book collation certification. Ancient short quotations only.

excerpts.finding: Complete working five paragraphs checked, including initial mountain and thanksgiving. I.2 that-you-fast bracketed; I.4 to-God bracketed. I.5 future complete a Gebhardt conjecture against reported Athos do. No Hermas happy-reply in I.3; raw source remains intact.

excerpts.transcription: ναι φημι κε μακαριον με ποιησεις εαν γνω την νηστειαν την δεκτην τω [θ]ω
excerpts.finding: Longer reply is preserved except damaged theta in final abbreviated divine name. Bonner reports Hamburg and Coptic support; reported Athos and Vulgata omit. Working editorial accents and nomen-sacrum expansion explicitly disclosed. Other differences: God for Lord at I.3 first speech, acceptable/complete reversed; lost lower page includes much of I.4/5; I.5 teleis may have faint accent. No wholesale replacement of working Greek.

excerpts.transcription: Felicem me facies, domine, si sciero quod ieiunium acceptum sit domino.
excerpts.finding: Direct Palatina corroboration of Hermas’s reply; says acceptable to Lord where Michigan God. Similar conditional ethical teaching follows. The final consummabis lacks the working great in this printed version.

Vulgata omits the happy-reply: teacher promise passes directly to audi. It retains the ethical conditions and future consummabis; final Lord differs from working God. It cannot be cited as supporting the restored reply.

All eleven historical paragraphs checked. Brackets at II.2/5/9 retained and disclosed. II.7 command-I-gave conjecture distinguished from Athos promise; II.9 householder subject inserted by Hollenberg from versions. Old reader50 had major silent narrative jumps, not a continuous text.

II.1 concerning-fasting marked for deletion by dots. II.2 most-faithful/pleasing-to-him/going-away differs from working faithful/pleasing/honored. II.2 instruction lines18–23 wholly supplied with no legible letters reported. A whole leaf then missing roughly II.3–8; cannot claim papyrus preserves central story. II.9 partly preserves householder and food-sent supplement. II.11 explicitly servant action, no food possessive, received retained. All damage/supplies distinct from omissions.

Palatina supplies continuous vineyard, freedom, extra work, son’s co-heir approval, meal, distribution, intercession and final approval. Names friends along with son at II.8 and sent-food wording at II.11. It differs from working Greek at stake-vines/fence and several constructions. It is one version tradition, not a second Greek witness.

Vulgata independently consulted printed continuous parable. Retains promised freedom, extra work, shared inheritance, food sharing and favor prayer. II.8 son and friends, II.9 calls friends, II.11 food sent; do not silently insert these details in working Greek. The two Latin versions must not be called independent manuscripts of identical Greek.
